_about: Social standing of the household a character grew up in. 'level' 0-6 feeds weighting elsewhere (entries with bias 'low' favor levels 0-2, 'high' favor 4-6). Written for DCUGen; original content.

tiers.label: Destitute
home: a shelter cot
a car parked behind a laundromat
a condemned row house
an encampment under an overpass
a single motel room rented by the week
a squat above a closed bakery
shaped: Learned early that a promise is worth exactly what is in your hand right now.
Still eats fast, hunched over the plate, as if someone might take it away.
Can read a room for danger in two seconds and can never quite switch that off.
Carries a quiet fury at people who waste food, money or kindness.
Feels like a fraud in any building with a doorman.
Knows every free clinic, soup line and warm library in three neighborhoods.

tiers.label: Poor
home: a crowded apartment in the projects
a trailer on cinder blocks
a walk-up with a broken buzzer
a shared house with two other families
rooms above the family's failing shop
shaped: Grew up counting coins at the register before every grocery run and still does the math in {their} head.
Treats a full refrigerator as a small miracle.
Is fiercely proud of anything earned and suspicious of anything given.
Learned to fix things rather than replace them, from shoes to car engines.
Distrusts landlords, bill collectors and anyone in a nice suit with a clipboard.
Knows that a neighbor with a casserole can matter more than a bank.

tiers.label: Working class
home: a narrow row house
a duplex near the rail yard
a small rental bungalow
a company-town cottage
a second-floor apartment over a hardware store
shaped: Believes in clocking in, doing the job and not making a fuss about it.
Respects calloused hands more than diplomas.
Thinks of overtime, layoffs and strikes as weather: something you plan around.
Has a deep loyalty to the block, the union hall and the team {they} grew up cheering for.
Is quietly embarrassed by people who complain about small problems.
Can talk to anyone on a loading dock or a factory floor as an equal.

tiers.label: Middle class
home: a split-level house on a cul-de-sac
a suburban ranch house with a basketball hoop
a condo near a decent school
a brick colonial with a mortgage the parents worried about
a tidy apartment in a safe neighborhood
shaped: Assumes, a little too easily, that the system mostly works.
Was expected to get good grades, go to college and have a backup plan for the backup plan.
Feels guilty about having had it easy and sometimes overcorrects.
Knows how to fill out forms, talk to teachers and navigate an office without fear.
Was sheltered enough that the first real danger came as a shock.
Has a soft spot for barbecues, minivans and other ordinary comforts.

tiers.label: Affluent
home: a large house in a gated suburb
a renovated brownstone
a lake house that became the family's main home
a doctor's colonial with a three-car garage
a modern glass home on a hill
shaped: Grew up with tutors, music lessons and a summer camp for every interest.
Is good at sounding confident in rooms full of important people.
Learned that most problems can be solved with a phone call to the right person.
Is still figuring out which friendships were real and which were about the pool.
Feels the weight of parents who expected a return on their investment.
Has never had to choose between rent and medicine, and sometimes forgets that others do.

tiers.label: Wealthy
home: a country estate with stables
a penthouse spanning two floors
an oceanfront compound
a historic mansion with a staff wing
a family townhouse in the most expensive part of the city
shaped: Was raised partly by nannies, drivers and household staff, and remembers their birthdays better than the parents'.
Is used to being recognized, photographed and flattered.
Knows the difference between old money and new money and pretends not to care.
Can order in four languages, sail a boat and ski, and has never done laundry.
Has a nagging fear of being liked only for the family name.
Treats money as a tool, not a goal, which only the rich can afford to do.

tiers.label: Elite
home: an ancestral estate with its own chapel
a private island compound
a skyscraper whose top floors belong to the family
a guarded embassy residence
a palace-sized mansion with a museum wing
shaped: Grew up among heads of state, tech founders and royalty as ordinary dinner guests.
Has never in their life waited in a line that wasn't optional.
Was groomed from birth to inherit a business, a title or a dynasty.
Has bodyguards in their earliest memories.
Sees cities as chessboards and people as pieces, and fights that instinct daily.
Knows that every scandal is survivable with enough lawyers, and that terrifies {them} a little.

shifts.text: The family's fortunes {rose|swelled} when a {small business|patent|lawsuit settlement|lottery ticket} paid off.
The family lost nearly everything in a market crash and never fully recovered.
A parent's medical bills ate the savings, one envelope at a time.
A plant closing took the family's main paycheck and the town's with it.
A distant relative's will moved the family into a nicer part of town.
A parent was promoted into management, and dinner conversations changed overnight.
A villain's rampage leveled the family business, and the insurance company called it an act of god.
A parent's gambling quietly drained what little the family had.
